replication_study.hypothesis: At the country-election level, the logged number of qualifying parties in the party system has a positive association with logged economic policy dispersion, measured as the distance between the most extreme party PCA scores.

data_plan.dataset_identifier: Supplied CMP_final.dta and CPDS_final.dta (Andrews-Money replication data)
data_plan.source_type: Comparative Manifesto Project party/election data merged with Comparative Political Data Set electoral-system data
data_plan.wave_or_subset: All available observations, as specified by task_input/replication_data/Andrews-Money_Replication.do; CMP data_sample labels include old countries/old timeframe, old countries/new timeframe, new countries/new timeframe, and additional potential observations.
data_plan.sample_size: 3,110 deduplicated CMP party-election records and 1,743 deduplicated CPDS records before merging; the executed script reports the final regression N in results/analysis_sample_summary.csv.
data_plan.unit_of_analysis: Country-election party system for the regression, constructed from party-election manifesto and seat records.
data_plan.access_details: Local files supplied in task_input/replication_data; no external access is required.

qualification.explanation: The supplied datasets directly support the same party-system construction, manifesto-category PCA, electoral-rule control, and country-clustered regression used for the claim, while providing a broader replication sample.
qualification.similarity_to_original: The original paper describes economic positions from a PCA of CMP categories 303, 401, 402, 403, 404, 407, 412, 413, 414, 504, 505, and 701 (original_paper.pdf, p. 814) and dispersion as the distance between extreme parties (pp. 815-816). CMP_final.dta contains exactly these per* fields, party seats, election dates, and country labels; CPDS_final.dta contains country-year proportional-system information. The supplied Andrews-Money_Replication.do applies these same variables and a country-clustered OLS model.
qualification.deviation_from_original: The paper reports policy positions for 20 countries from 1945 to 1999 (original_paper.pdf, p. 814), whereas the supplied CMP data include 29 countries and data_sample groups extending through 2018 (inspection of CMP_final.dta). The supplied do-file explicitly directs the replication to use all available observations, so this is a new, expanded sample rather than the paper's original scope.

data_plan.notes: The supplied do-file's two sequential party-screening operations are implemented literally. PCA is fit on complete records for its 12 economic-manifesto inputs, and regression uses complete country-election systems.

planned_method.steps: Deduplicate each supplied Stata file; merge CMP party-election records to CPDS by country and election year; create ordered country-election IDs; retain parties according to the two consecutive-seat-share screening steps in the supplied do-file; count retained parties; derive the first economic PCA score; calculate the within-system extreme-party distance; log both focal measures; construct single-member and lagged-dispersion controls; fit clustered OLS.
planned_method.models: Ordinary least squares with country-clustered robust covariance, matching the supplied Stata command reg dispersion count_parties single_member lagged_dispersion, cluster(id_country).
planned_method.outcome_variable: Natural log of economic dispersion: the within-country-election maximum minus minimum first-component economic-policy score.
planned_method.independent_variables: Natural log of the count of qualifying parties in the country-election party system.
planned_method.control_variables: Single-member-district indicator (prop == 0) and lagged logged dispersion.
planned_method.tools_software: Python 3 with pandas/Stata reader, scikit-learn PCA, and statsmodels OLS.

planned_estimation_and_test.estimation: The coefficient on logged party count in the economic-dispersion regression.
planned_estimation_and_test.test: Two-sided 95% cluster-robust confidence interval using a t critical value with country clusters minus one degrees of freedom; the hypothesis is supported if the coefficient and lower confidence bound are positive.

planned_method.missing_data_handling: PCA scores are assigned only to complete 12-category manifesto records. Systems with missing/nonfinite logged dispersion, controls, or lag are excluded listwise from OLS.
planned_method.multiple_testing_policy: No multiplicity correction: this replication tests the single preregistered economic-dimension hypothesis.
planned_method.inference_criteria: Support requires a positive focal coefficient and a 95% country-clustered confidence interval excluding zero in the positive direction.

files.replicate_analysis.py: Executable analysis script. It reads the two supplied .dta files using relative paths, implements the supplied Stata replication workflow, saves a machine-readable JSON result and CSV coefficient/sample-summary tables in results/, prints a concise summary, and raises an error on failure.

codebase.notes: Only replicate_analysis.py is executed. Input data and the original Stata do-file remain under task_input/; output files are generated at runtime under results/.

other: Other necessary software (e.g., git, make, wget)

analysis.instructions: From the workspace root, install requirements with pip install -r requirements.txt and run python replicate_analysis.py. Read results/replication_results.json for the focal inference and results/model_coefficients.csv for all model terms.
analysis.comparison_metrics: Compare the focal logged-party-count coefficient's sign, clustered robust standard error, 95% confidence interval, and statistical conclusion with the supplied claim (reported original coefficient 0.39 and robust SE 0.14).
